title: QQ plot

blocks.what_we_do: Compare the distribution of observed autosomal association p-values with a uniform-null reference.
blocks.why: A quantile-quantile (QQ) plot pairs ordered observed values with the values expected under a reference distribution. Under calibrated null tests, p-values are approximately uniform; -log10 transforms small values into large positive values. A few strong associations lift the extreme tail. Broad deviation can reflect confounding, technical problems, model misspecification or many true small effects. A visual deviation alone cannot distinguish them. Correlated variants also mean the points are not independent observations.
blocks.command:
```{r s7-1}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
autosomal <- results$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.1", "qq.png"), function() plot_qq(results$P[autosomal], "Adjusted simulated GWAS: autosomal QQ plot"))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
Most points are close to the null diagonal, with a strong upper-tail departure. Missing, zero or invalid p-values are not plotted as arbitrary significant values.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Does a strong departure affecting only the extreme tail necessarily imply genome-wide confounding?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. A few true signals can lift the tail while most null tests remain calibrated.

</details>

figures.gemini_prompt: Draw a teaching QQ schematic showing a diagonal null distribution, a tail-only departure and broad inflation in separate labelled panels. Explain possible causes without labelling every departure confounding; use line styles and text as well as colour.
figures.alt_text: Most adjusted autosomal tests follow the null diagonal, with an upper-tail departure from a few association signals.
